validated_results.title: Urinary phytoestrogen excretion and prostate cancer risk: a nested case-control study in the Multiethnic Cohort.
validated_results.reason: This nested case-control study examines urinary genistein excretion in relation to incident prostate cancer risk with multivariable-adjusted effect estimates.

sample_size.excerpt: This included 249 matched sets, 94 with one control and 155 with two controls (249 cases and 404 controls).
sample_size.location: Materials and methods, Case ascertainment and control selection, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 249 + 404 = 653

cases.excerpt: Urine samples were analysed for daidzein, genistein, equol, and enterolactone among 249 incident prostate cancer cases and 404 controls matched on age, race/ethnicity, date/time of specimen collection, and fasting status.
cases.location: Materials and methods, Case ascertainment and control selection, paragraph 1

p_value.excerpt: There was a nonsignificant inverse trend for genistein ( P trend =0.09), for daidzein+genistein combined ( P trend =0.07), and for equol ( P trend =0.08).

design.excerpt: We carried out a nested case–control study within the Multiethnic Cohort Study
design.location: Materials and methods, Study population and data collection, paragraph 1

timing.excerpt: A prospective biospecimen subcohort was developed, largely between 2001 and 2006, when cohort members who gave informed consent to participate provided a blood and/or urine sample.
timing.location: Materials and methods, Study population and data collection, paragraph 1

continent.excerpt: This case–control study is nested within a large multiethnic cohort in Hawaii and California.

location.excerpt: nested within a large multiethnic cohort in Hawaii and California

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Daidzein, genistein, equol, and enterolactone were analysed by HPLC with electrospray ionization tandem mass spectrometry using isotopically labelled internal standards of all four analytes
exposure_measurement.location: Materials and methods, Laboratory assays, paragraph 1
